title: Shared spot removal produces apparent dip coupling in released TESS CPV measurements
abstract: We test whether separate dips in complex periodic variables change together. Released per-rotation depths give a mean one-rotation correlation of 0.180 (95 percent star-bootstrap interval 0.128 to 0.232) in 61 stars and 167 sectors. The shared harmonic background fit mixes dip amplitudes. An explicit linear correction under fixed box profiles changes the mean to -0.064 (-0.112 to -0.014). Broader profiles also remove the positive mean. In independent Gaussian sawtooth injections on real stellar backgrounds, measured correlation is 0.178 but input correlation is -0.058. Known-profile recovery gives -0.060, with a paired recovery error consistent with zero. Projection identities and 395 synthetic geometry checks verify the implementation. This result identifies a measurement confounder and supplies a correction method. It does not establish physical anticorrelation or exclude shared material supply. Unknown dip shapes, unequal cadence weights and selected persistent features limit physical inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps are included.
